newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates close steady amid low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates close steady amid low demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady amid low demand from spinners, who are waiting for fresh yarn export orders, dealers said.

Also helping to head off any price rise were figures from the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association showing that output had fallen only 2.39 percent to 7.366 million 375-lb bales by January 1 in the 1996/97 (July-June) crop year from 7.547 million bales in the year-ago period.
Rates rose last week on fears that 1996/97 production might be reach only 8.5 million bales, compared to official estimates of 9.2 million, dealers said.
In the kerb market, the rate for NIAB-78 fluctuated between 2,400 and 2,425 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), one dealer said. Rates were likely to open steady on Monday, he added.
